change_summary: Ran paired backtests with the repo venv and the repaired snapshot archive for `A+B` versus `A+B+C` on three windows: `2025-10-23 -> 2026-04-20`, `2025-04-22 -> 2025-10-21`, and `2024-10-01 -> 2025-04-30`. No strategy code changed between runs; only the enabled strategy set differed. The result was regime-dependent and failed the majority-window stability test, so C was not re-enabled by default.

delta_metrics.note: C helped only in the ripping-bull window. It hurt the primary window and failed the weak-window guardrails materially. This does not satisfy AGENTS.md Gate 4 majority-window stability.
delta_metrics.window_2_guardrail_failure: A+B+C produced both negative return (-9.66%) and negative sharpe_daily (-0.83) despite a mathematically positive EV product

hypothesis: Once full historical P-ERN snapshots exist, re-enabling `earnings_event_long` should improve the joint system more reliably than it did under the partial-data regime. The test compared the repaired `A+B+C` stack against the current `A+B` baseline across three non-overlapping windows using the same repaired archive and no other rule changes.
next_retry_requires: Do not retry `C strategy revival` on the thesis 'more earnings snapshots alone will fix it'
If C is revisited, propose a genuinely new mechanism such as event grading or a stricter slot-allocation interaction, then re-test against the repaired archive
Shift the default alpha priority toward `LLM soft ranking` once replay coverage materially increases
notes: This failure matters because it closes the old ambiguity. P-ERN was a real measurement blocker, but it was not the sole root cause of C's instability.
rejection_reason: Rejected on Gate 4 multi-window stability. Full historical snapshots were necessary to evaluate C credibly, but data repair alone did not make `earnings_event_long` a stable system-level alpha source.
